   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!

From: Mark Payne, COVENTRY


Dear Ron and Brian,

Many thanks for including my
letter in Issue 56. I am still
unable to get a printout using
the database program.

As I sent you a printout of the
listing last time and that did
not seem of much help, I will do
as you ask and I will send you
the entire program so you can
see for yourself.

I contacted the person who wrote

and he could not help as he did
not have a printer to try it on.

get this program to work,could
you please help me get a small
program that I can insert into
TASWORD 2 that will do a sort as
I can get a printout using
Tasword.

            Regards,

              Mark

Brian Cavers to Mark Payne

It seems the program you sent is
probably set to use the printer
port of a particular Spectrum
direct from machine code and so
cannot be easily adapted. It
seems O.K. up to that point.

Anyway, I've now written a new
program to sort Tasword files
called TEXSORT and this should
appear in next month's OUTLET.
I have sent you an advance copy
which you should have received
by now.

                        - Brian

From: Les Tyler, CHELTENHAM

This is a hint that might prove
useful to UNIDOS owners, it
seems to work very well on my
set-up(128K Sinclair/ DISCIPLE).
I, like many others I suspect,
have never been able to access a
'faulty' sector on a disc that
produces the 'Sector Error..'
report, in order to correct it.
The LOAD @ and SAVE @ commands
in GDOS only work for me when
there is no error present which
is NOT when I need to use them!
The only remedy normally avail-
able has been to re-format the
disc and copy the relevant files
over from a back-up source,
which can be time-consuming to
say the least when there are a
lot of files on the disc.

My usual routine, therefore,
when a 'Sector Error' occurred,
was to make a fresh copy of the
disc, put the faulty one aside
till I needed it again and then
re-format several discs at once.

Fairly recently, I installed
UNIDOS Version 2 in my DISCIPLE,
which has its own FORMAT
routine, providing 6 options.
Options 3 and 4, (which I have
found very useful in themselves
as they re-format a disc without
losing the existing contents),
have, in addition, a hidden
virtue. When one of my discs
produced the 'Sector Error' for
the first time, I decided to try
these options just to see if
they copied the faulty sector
across to the new disc.

I could not see any other result
ensuing. Imagine my surprise,
therefore, when the transfer
routine did NOT stop with the
'Sector Error' message, as it
would have done with GDOS. In
addition, the transferred files
had no apparent errors in them,
the programs loading and running
as normal!

I had about 6 discs lined up for
re-formatting, so I tried the
technique on all of them, and
they ALL finished up OK. Need-
less to say I was delighted with
the result ! I have no idea why
this should happen, but my guess
is that the cause of the 'Sector
Error' is probably something
very simple, like a wrongly-set
single bit that GDOS does not

like, but that UNIDOS seems to
ignore. It is clearly not a
major garbling of the stored
data else the resulting programs
would not run.

Please note that this is NOT a
universal panacea for disc/
sector errors, it does not work
for errors in the directory
tracks, (0-3), or for the
'Sector Missing' error, which
may be peculiar to UNIDOS.
Nevertheless, it seems like a
good idea when coming across the
'Sector Error' message to try
this out before attempting more
drastic measures. Also note that
I was using twin-drives, with
the FORMAT routine being held on
one drive, and the action taking
place on the other.

I will have to wait until I get
the error again before being
able to try it out on a single
drive! I would be interested to
know if others find this useful,
or can offer an explanation of
how UNIDOS manages to refresh
the parts that GDOS cannot!

            Cheers!

           Les Tyler

Brian Cavers to Les Tyler


Mmmm... interesting. Are you
saying that even the files that
would not load would load from
the new disc once copied across
using UNIDOS? If so, my guess is
that the error may be in the
first sector header which seems
to duplicate info in the direct-
ory (presumably to make things
easier for some routine in GDOS)
but which UNIDOS ignores.

                        - Brian

I hope you do not mind if I
throw in a few comments on last
month's letters! Firstly, Mr.
Jacks' mammoth offering.

Disc drives are not usually
alignable by the user. They
need sophisticated test gear.
The datum point for a drive is
usually  track zero. There is
normally a photoelectric
sensor for this. However, the
stepper motor itself has to be
aligned first, so that each
step actually coincides with
the position of a physical
track on a test disc.

Alignment can be costly and with
new bare drives being offered at
under `40 these days, it's
probably cheaper to replace it.

Spectrum +2 keyboards are
available. I think the spare's
price is just short of `30. They
do not sell the membranes
though. Make sure you get a REAL
+2 one, as the +2A ones are not
the same! If you have troubles,
please contact me.(B G Services)

Next, Pro-Pac PD. This library
is run by just one person. I
know this as he shared a stand
with me at the last All Formats
show. The lack of replies, I
cannot comment on but we did
have a long chat.

Firstly, he has had a lot of
problems getting some of the
software to run on all flavours
of Spectrum. (Ask Brian Cavers
about this, he probably has
nightmares about it!). The non
running software was probably
for this reason.

Delays in supply -though I think
one month was what he admitted
to - was due to two causes. The
first was a batch of incredibly
duff 3" discs. Secondly, he
completely underestimated the
demand and the work involved!

He says that to date, he only
has had two letters of
complaint, one from Mr Parnell,
and one other.

He has recently done some work
for me, which was totally
satisfactory so if anyone out
there is still having trouble,
please let me know, and I will
bend his ear for you!

Propac is suspended right now,
as he is doing his GCSEs so he
has cancelled his ads.

Interleave on Disks. The
Formatter used by OUTLET for the
+3 uses this technique to speed
loading. Chris Pile, who wrote
'Hiformat' for them, also wrote
a program called 'Iformat' that
allows you to fiddle with the
interleave, though it only gives
the 173K space.
                        - Brian

I use an original Spectrum 128K
(i.e., no built-in tape or disc)
with a +D disc drive interface
and single drive and have a
"Serial 8056" printer connected
via the 128K built in RS232
socket. The problems are as
follows.

1) Whenever I use 128K Advanced
Art Studio and select Kempston
Joystick control, I in fact end
up with no control with the
arrow flashing hopelessly in the
middle of the screen. The
program works correctly from the
keyboard when that option is
selected.

I have enclosed a snapshot of
the offending program.I've tried
loading it without the joystick,
the disc interface, the Kempston
interface and also on a +2 with
no improvement. Any ideas?

2) Still with the Advanced Art
Studio - do you know what has to
be changed in the program to
allow, if possible, screen files
to be LOADed and SAVEd via +D
instead of a tape transfer?

3) My next problem concerns my
printer. I would like to be able
to print straight from OUTLET,
using the built-in RS232 port,
but I do not know how to. Mine
is a rather limited printer but
it was bought with my Spectrum

in one of those "Dixons" deals
so I hoped a reader had perhaps
bought the same and mastered it.

4) Finally, why can I not print
a screen dump direct from Art
Studio when I can print a screen
using RANDOMIZE USR 63696 which
is a routine in the printer
software?

       Yours faithfully,

        Brian Kinsley

To Brian Kinsley from Brian Gaff

You do have problems! Let me go
through your letter point by
point.I do not think I can solve
everything, but in most cases, I
think I can see the problems.

1. Well, all I can do is say
   that you must have a problem
   with your machine or
   interface, as the Kempston
   port in my Multiface 1 works
   fine on your snapshot!

2. Your best bet here is to
   contact INDUG. The code
   needed to save and load to
   MDV is totally different to
   that required by the +D, so
   it would really need a patch
   of some kind.

   I know that the standard Art
   Studio has been hacked. [see
   also letter from Danny Beach]


3. The first thing to do is to
   run the +D config program and
   de-select the +D printer port
   Make sure you use this SYS
   file whenever you need to
   print anything. I no longer
   have a working 128K, but it
   looks to me that the +3
   option could be modified.
   Basically, replace FORMAT
   LINE with FORMAT "p",baud,
   and FORMAT LPRINT "U" etc,
   with POKE 23349, 39:POKE
   23350, 1. Hopefully, it
   should then work![around line
   1400 in the "CONTENTS" BASIC]

4. This goes back to no.2, I
   think. I cannot tell if it is
   set for Interface 1, but I
   suspect it could be. Other-
   wise, it may be that using
   the new SYS file I mentioned
   in 3 above, may make it work.

I do think though, that the 8056
is going to cause you trouble.
It is in fact a printer origin-
ally designed for a portable
IBM. This probably means that
its graphics emulation is IBM,
rather than Epson. Sorry to be
so negative here, we have
published your full address as
requested so maybe someone read-
ing this has some new answers.

                             BG

Dear Ron and Brian,

Thanks once again for your
wonderful work in OUTLET. First
a few comments about previous
letters....

a) Thank you Malcolm Perry for
your explanation about connect-
-ing two different drives and
above all for making my night -
mares about changing "jumper
blocks" at the back of drives go
away ! Just one other problem
Malcolm... how possible is it to
connect up two Spectrum setups
(e.g. like my own, two Speccy
128+'s with a +D on one, and a

DISCiPLE on the other) to one
twin 3 1/2 DSDD (MGT Lifetime)
drive and have both Spectrum's
sharing the drive at the same
time. Obviously, with both being
connected both could not use,say
drive 1 simultaneously but could
one use drive one and the other
use drive 2? What sort of
connector/switch is needed? Any
ideas please?

b) About Mr Vincent L Jack's
letter (Issue 57): please feel
free to contact me at the above
address as I think I can help
you with 4 of your points.
(2,3,4, and 9... disc program
compressor,sector error problems
Art studio 128, and Unidos
difficulties).

c) I was fascinated by Mr Carlo
Malantrucco's letter about this
program which allows him to LOAD
from DISCiPLE discs on his Opus
DISCovery. Any Opus owners
wishing to contact me to swap
programs on DISCiPLE disc (3 1/2
DSDD) or simply ideas, please
feel free to write.

Say, if Opus users can read
DISCiPLE discs then why can't
DISCiPLE/+D owners read programs
of Opus discs?!!! Anybody got a
program that could do that, or
does anybody around have enough
know-how about DISCiPLE/+D's and
Opus's to be able to write a
program? Why should certain
programs written on certain disc
systems be unavailable to other
disc systems, eh?

d) About Mr. J.P. Messenbird's
letter about the lack of Speccy
software about, I'd like to put
the following points:

i) Facts have to be faced. The
fact is the Speccy is gradually
dying.... Is there any reason
why OUTLET could not publish a
few previously-released titles
of software from software houses
that are now more concerned with
other computers? The way the
Speccy will survive that little
while longer is by going higher
tech and becoming a more disc-
based machine with, for example,
the +D. There would surely be
the demand to see old previously
released software re-released,
but for new drive systems.

It does not necessarily have to
be games but they do make up a
large proportion of software!
Maybe not so much for +3 owners
who have enjoyed limited support
from software producers like
Ocean, but I speculate if OUTLET
were to boast in next month's
issue for +D/DISCiPLE/OPUS there
was some ex-full price game(like
Op Wolf) loads of extra people
would subscribe as well as the
existing "serious" readership.

ii) There's loads of software
for the Speccy around which many
people have not heard or seen!!
I talked to loads of people at
the recent European Computer
trade show in London, and it's a
crime to learn how many "nearly
completed" titles they have in

stock which will never see the
light of day. Now is the time to
empty all these closets and this
is what I am presently trying to
do, by twisting arms of a few
publishers. Grab hold of those
programs now and get 'em into
OUTLET so we can all share them.

e) Anybody connected with SD
Software reading this? Do you
know how I can get in contact
with Steve Warr, Brian?
Anybody any ideas on getting a
+D or DISCiPLE or either with
UNIDOS, connected up to a High
Density 3 1/2 drive? I know the
hardware in the two interfaces
(i.e the drive controller)
should handle the high density
drive, but obviously the ROM
software would need adapting.

Surely, as high density drives
are coming down in price, this
would be a good enough adapt-
ation to justify production of a
VERS 3 Unidos chip?

Anybody out there with Unidos
want details on how to have both
your new Unidos chip and your
old GDOS/G+DOS chip inside your
case at the same time? Both the
chips are instantly swapped at
the flick of a switch when
powering down. Once again..
contact me at the above address
for details.

Keep up the good work Ron and
Brian!
          Best wishes,
                   Danny Beach.

Brian Cavers to Danny Beach

I sometimes wonder myself what
happens to copyright if a soft-
ware company goes bust. However,
where the company is still
trading,even if writing software
for another computer,there is no
way that they would tolerate us
having their Spectrum games in
OUTLET without an agreement.
SINCLAIR USER and YOUR SINCLAIR
pay large sums to put old games
on their front cover tapes.

Yes, there's lots and lots of
Spectrum software around that
many have not seen. It's wasted
but it's doubtful permission
would be given to put it into
OUTLET without paying royalties.

I don't know who Steve Warr is,
Danny. If he is at SD SOFTWARE
then why not write? SD are at
70 Rainhall Road, Barnoldswick,
Lancashire, BB8 6AB.

Thanks for all the info! We have
had several readers asking about
converting ART STUDIO 128 to +D/
Disciple use. If you have done
this conversion can you provide
details or better yet, send the
code or program whatever that
modifies, POKEs it etc. so I can
put it in OUTLET. That would be
great.
                        Brian
